chapter: Regional bands, politics and travel abroad
title: Working for Erskine Tate and Hinton's memories of the Vendome Theater
summary: Wilson played club dates for the considerate Tate, and Hinton recalls Tate's all-star pit orchestra at the Vendome in 1923.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I was just thinking, even though we're jumping back and forth in the '30s between Chicago and New York, did you have any escapades, any association with Erskine Tate out there in Chicago?
Yes, I worked for Erskine many times. Triangle Club, on the West Side, and then on other occasions with --
That knock on the door was your son Steven coming back in. So nice to see him again. (Inaudible) last night and this beautiful young man, a drummer, it's nice to see you.
We were talking about Erskine Tate there in Chicago.
Yeah, I played with Erskine, several club dates, I guess.
I enjoyed working for him. He was a very nice man. I never heard him play his violin, I think he told me that was his instrument. He fronted the band, but he sure was a good leader.
Yeah. He sure knew how he wanted the music to go, and he was really nice to musicians, too.
Yeah, very considerate sort of man. He never said anything sarcastic, never raised his voice to any of the guys in the band. You know, club dates, they weren't so perfect, you know.

I can remember clear back when I was 13 years old in Chicago, 1923, Chicago on a Sunday afternoon, everybody went to the Vendome, the black people in our community went to the Vendome Theater to see Erskine Tate's orchestra. He opened up with an overture, ______, something like that. And he had Louie Armstrong then, Eddie South was in the band, and ______, a good clarinet player, Barney Bigard, these great guys. Teddy Welford was the pianist before Earl Hines and ______ the great drummer.
So these were the ones that we followed. Of course, you later got to play with him.
Those bands that Erskine had were very unusual for theater bands, weren't they?
To have an all-star soloist in a pit band like that.
